CHAVI Client

Stage Information¶

The Stage Information module records the cancer staging details for each diagnosis. This information is crucial for determining the extent of disease and treatment planning.

Data Collection Fields¶

Staging System¶

  • Staging System: The classification system used (e.g., TNM 8th Edition, FIGO)

  • Stage Type: Type of staging information (e.g., clinical, pathological)

TNM Classification¶

  • T Stage: Description of the primary tumor

    • Prefix: Clinical (c) or Pathological (p)

    • Category: T0, T1, T2, T3, T4

    • Suffix: Modifiers (a, b, c) if applicable

  • N Stage: Description of regional lymph node involvement

    • Prefix: Clinical (c) or Pathological (p)

    • Category: N0, N1, N2, N3

    • Suffix: Modifiers (a, b, c) if applicable

  • M Stage: Description of distant metastasis

    • Prefix: Clinical (c) or Pathological (p)

    • Category: M0, M1

    • Suffix: Modifiers (a, b, c) if applicable

Overall Stage¶

  • Overall Stage: Combined stage grouping (e.g., Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, Stage IV)

Special Considerations¶

  1. Staging accuracy:

    1. Use the most current staging system version

    2. Document the basis for staging (clinical vs. pathological)

    3. Update staging as new information becomes available

  2. TNM documentation:

    1. Include all relevant prefixes and suffixes

    2. Document any uncertainty in staging

    3. Note any special circumstances affecting staging

  3. Multiple primaries:

    1. Stage each primary tumor separately

    2. Clearly link staging to specific diagnosis

    3. Document any interactions between multiple primaries

  4. Stage migration:

    1. Record dates of staging changes

    2. Document reasons for stage changes

    3. Maintain history of previous staging
